info.title: Ordinary business entry HTTP contract
info.description: A02A module-root conditional catalog. Each entry binds client_id, login_entry_id, tenant policy and Business purpose. No device, scan or OIDC routes. Cookie name/path, origin, token lifetime and mount prefix belong to the host profile. JSON/form bodies are limited to 16384 bytes; all responses use Cache-Control: no-store. Secrets never belong in query parameters. Fixed and Choose are mutually exclusive; registration requires Fixed plus explicit enablement and email service. Password recovery is account-wide and appears only when account security and recovery email are both enabled.

post.description: Exact configured Origin AND x-embedded-idp-browser: 1 required; Sec-Fetch-Site, when supplied, must be same-origin. Tenant header forbidden. Refresh cookie is HttpOnly, Secure in HTTPS, SameSite=Strict, entry-specific name/path. Only access token appears in JSON. Browser selection route is present even for Fixed but selection is rejected by policy. Restore rotates; refresh requires expected_session. Logout without cookie is idempotent 204 in normal mode. Development restricted browser mode disables restore/refresh and requires expected_session even for cookie-less logout.

post.description: Anonymous account-wide recovery; it is not tenant- or entry-scoped. Strict JSON rejects unknown fields and query parameters; tenant and business selector headers are rejected. Bearer tokens and refresh cookies do not authenticate this operation, and no response sets or clears cookies. Bodies are limited to 16384 bytes and read within 5 seconds. Start has one deliberately uniform result for known, unknown, and ineligible email addresses: success means the request was recorded, not that email was sent or an account exists. Start uses the shared account budget as an abuse limit, not as authenticated identity. Outer host admission may read the start body and consume this budget before the browser Origin guard runs. A result with completed=false is not proof that a command did not commit.

post.description: Requires the exact configured Origin and x-embedded-idp-browser: 1; when present, Sec-Fetch-Site must be same-origin. Tenant and business selection headers are forbidden. The configured HttpOnly refresh cookie is read only; this route does not refresh or expose credentials. Strict JSON requires expected {tenant_id,account_id,session_id,client_id}; optional limit is 1..50 and cursor is at most 1024 encoded bytes. The host must bind identity purpose and restricted-session lifetime exactly to BrowserSessionHttpConfig. The current actor must be a first-party scope=null session; same-account delegated sessions remain listable. Request body limit is 16384 bytes. Response fields match SelfSessionPage and all responses are no-store.

get.description: Requires exactly one Bearer Authorization header. An optional x-embedded-idp-tenant-id must match the authenticated tenant; x-embedded-idp-business-id is rejected. The authenticated actor must be a current first-party session with scope=null; OAuth-derived scope-bearing sessions cannot authorize global self-security reads. Lists all of the same account's database-active sessions across tenants, including delegated scope-bearing sessions. Expired-by-time sessions are projected as status=expired; revoked/pending records are omitted. Cursor is base64url JSON version=1 with subject_id, tenant_id and canonical UUID session_id, at most 1024 encoded bytes. Query accepts only limit and cursor. Response contains no scope, refresh-token data or account email.
